title: Production trace replay and stochastic latency profiling for benchmark harness
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Add a production-trace replay mode and stochastic latency profiling to the benchmark harness so we can reliably detect regressions caused by kernel selection, attention path changes, and prefill/decode scheduling. This ticket implements: 1) a trace ingestion and normalization pipeline (supporting sampled request traces from Hosted API logs), 2) a deterministic replay driver that can inject real-world token distributions and request inter-arrival patterns into the microbench runner, and 3) an offline stochastic latency profiler that computes P50/P95/P99 across repeated replays with noise models (network, scheduling jitter). The goal is to surface regression signals that synthetic microbenchmarks miss (e.g., prefill/decoding interplay, rare long-tail kv-cache path switches) and to produce golden baseline artifacts that CI can compare against using multi-quantile gates and auto-rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Trace ingestion tool accepts gzip'd JSON traces and produces normalized replay bundles
Replay driver runs traces against existing bench harness and reproduces token-level timing (within a noise tolerance) for prefill and decode phases
Stochastic profiler runs N trials and emits P50/P95/P99 latency distributions and a summary HTML report uploaded to perf-dashboard
New CI job 'bench_trace_replay' executes on runtime PRs, compares distributions to golden baseline using configurable thresholds and fails PRs on sustained regressions
Golden baseline snapshot format and storage location documented; baseline version pinned to release tags and accessible by engineers and SREs
comments: 2025-02-21 — Kickoff: aligned with Perf WG on need for production traces — key motivators: intermittent 200-500ms tail increases observed in Hosted API (incident IN-2025-01). Action: sample 0.5% of live requests, scrub PII, export to s3://redwood-perf/traces/2025-02/

2025-02-25 — Prototype: first replay driver implemented (deterministic token timing) but observed mismatch on long-tail when kernel fallback occurs — suspected non-deterministic kernel selection in runtime; opened ENG-17902 to track kernel-selection determinism

2025-02-28 — Design review with Runtime team: decided to implement an injected scheduler jitter model rather than change live kernel scheduler for now to allow reproducible CI runs. Trade-off: may mask extreme scheduler bugs but accelerates iteration for regression detection.
2025-03-01 — PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4682 — Adds trace ingestion and normalization plus replay CLI. Need review from @sophia.nguyen (runtime) and @kenji.honda (bench infra).

2025-03-03 — Early results: replay of 10k sampled requests from a chat workload showed a 12% increase in P99 for decode when running model-variant quantized-8 compared to baseline. Uploaded report to perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboard/reports/trace-replay-2025-03-03

2025-03-04 — CI integration plan reviewed. Decided on multi-quantile gate thresholds (P50 delta 10%, P95 delta 12%, P99 delta 8%) and require 3/5 regression trials before failing a PR to reduce flakiness. Added flaky-test mitigation: re-run job automatically up to 2 times.

2025-03-05 — Blocker discovered: some traces include large user messages that trigger different attention tiling; added a trace normalization step to cap message size or bucket by sequence-length distribution. Follow-up: add sequence-length stratification to replay bundles.
